title: Objects stay whole in Rexx; flatten only at an explicit external boundary
summary: The Workbench keeps live ooRexx objects intact while objects, tools and API context coexist. Rexx-native instrumentation records those live references. LlmCodingBoundaryAdapter is the deliberate projection point for JSON/API/logging edges. dev14 closes the remaining compatibility-codec bypass by making LlmCodingJsonCodec delegate outbound turn projection to the boundary adapter.
invariants: Internal observation retains actual Rexx object identity rather than reconstructing meaning from flattened dictionaries, JSON or strings.
Python is not a Workbench semantic/controller or instrumentation layer; external-process transport may use non-Rexx machinery only where the external boundary requires it.
Outbound turn projection has one authority: LlmCodingBoundaryAdapter.
A compatibility API must delegate to the boundary rather than creating a second projection implementation.
Tests may use a spy boundary that projects for assertion, but production Workbench orchestration must not flatten a turn before the boundary.
procedure: Instrument object reads, tool calls/results, model/API turns and verification evidence in Rexx.
Carry the exact LlmCodingTurn object to an object-aware transport.
Project to Directory/JSON only when constructing an external API/logging payload.
For compatibility encoding, inject or use LlmCodingBoundaryAdapter rather than calling turn~asDirectory directly.

provenance.claim: Rexx-native trace events retain live subject/context references; summaries are explicit projections.
Explicit external projection boundary for turns and trace summaries.
dev14 compatibility codec delegates turn JSON projection to the configured boundary.
Regression checks that the exact live turn reaches the compatibility codec boundary before projection.
